If two conclusions are represented by the same non-terminal symbol in the compressed grammar, they are merged. The compression is re-run after any significant belief change.", "scope": {"covers": ["systems with a large, structured belief base", "conclusions expressible in a formal language"], "excludes": ["systems with very few beliefs where compression is trivial", "conclusions that are not amenable to syntactic pattern detection"]}, "forbidden": [{"case": "Two conclusions map to the same non-terminal in the compressed grammar but have different truth conditions in an edge case not yet encountered by the system, leading to a contradiction when that edge case arises.", "eval": "program:compression_collision_detector"}], "prose_notes": "This criterion is syntactic but leverages latent semantic structure through compression. Eager merging risks grouping unrelated claims that happen to share surface patterns. Reluctant merging risks failing to recognize deep structural identity, causing redundancy."}
